question: Should `sessions.list` become a publicly capped, successful-and-truncated gateway operation at 1000, or should existing callers retain unbounded RPC semantics while the shipped agent tool is bounded separately?
rationale: The patch changes behavior for valid protocol inputs above 1000; only maintainers can choose the durable gateway API and upgrade contract.

options.title: Adopt the server-side cap
options.body: Keep the resolver clamp, make the effective-limit and paging contract visible to gateway consumers, and prove that clients can recover all rows using pagination.

options.title: Limit only the agent tool
options.body: Preserve the public RPC’s existing semantics and bound the shipped tool path instead, accepting that separate RPC hardening would still need a future design.

recommendation.title: Adopt the server-side cap
recommendation.body: Keep the resolver clamp, make the effective-limit and paging contract visible to gateway consumers, and prove that clients can recover all rows using pagination.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged gateway-bound work provides the closest visible precedent for selecting a consistent parameter-bound policy.
